summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and coronary artery disease presented with fever and shortness of breath from dialysis. She was found to have culture-negative sepsis, a type 2 NSTEMI with rising troponins and EKG changes, and an acute GI bleed from a gastric polyp requiring epinephrine injection. She developed transient confusion likely due to uremia, which resolved after dialysis. An episode of asymptomatic ventricular tachycardia occurred, managed with IV amiodarone, though it was discontinued due to QTc prolongation. Calciphylaxis in her thighs was treated with wound care and intralesional sodium thiosulfate, while IV therapy was avoided due to arrhythmia risk. Antibiotics were adjusted based on clinical course and dialysis needs. She stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged to extended care with optimized medications, including fentanyl for pain, cinacalcet, and avoidance of QT-prolonging and calciphylaxis-exacerbating agents.
